{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793006052027,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_018ARShyzjHETMTEFMnQz5qc","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA Cholesky decomposition.\n//\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular.\n// A is stored in row-major order in the reference algorithm; the result L is\n// identical in structure (lower triangular, zero upper part).\n//\n// Parallel decomposition:\n//   * MPI:    rows are distributed cyclically over ranks (global row i is owned by\n//             rank i % P and stored as local row i / P), which balances the\n//             triangular workload. Validation and output gathering use MPI.\n//   * CUDA:   each rank keeps its rows on its GPU (column-major). The dominant\n//             work (dot products against already-factored columns) and the panel\n//             solve run as CUDA kernels.\n//   * OpenMP: host-side work (matrix generation, layout conversion, validation).\n//\n// Algorithm: blocked left-looking Cholesky. Columns are factored in panels of\n// kPanel columns. For every element, the reduction over k is accumulated in the\n// same ascending order as the original unblocked algorithm, so results match\n// the sequential reference up to floating-point contraction.\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr size_t kPanel = 64;  // number of columns factored per panel\n\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                              \\\n    do {                                                                              \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                    \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,          \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                        \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                             \\\n        }                                                                             \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Number of global rows owned by `rank` for an n-row matrix distributed over `size` ranks.\nsize_t localRowCount(size_t n, int rank, int size) {\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    return n > r ? (n - r + p - 1) / p : 0;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CUDA kernels\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// accD[a][b] = sum_{k<j0} piv[a][k] * piv[b][k]   for b <= a (panel diagonal block,\n// partial sums over the already-factored prefix). Data is replicated on all ranks.\n__global__ void kPivotDiag(const double* __restrict__ piv, int ldp, int j0, int w,\n                           double* __restrict__ accD) {\n    const int b = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int a = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (a >= w || b >= w || b > a) return;\n    const double* pa = piv + static_cast<size_t>(a) * ldp;\n    const double* pb = piv + static_cast<size_t>(b) * ldp;\n    double s = 0.0;\n    for (int k = 0; k < j0; ++k) s += pa[k] * pb[k];\n    accD[a * w + b] = s;\n}\n\n// accE[r][c] = sum_{k<j0} L[r][k] * piv[c][k] for local rows r >= rStart.\n// Local matrix is column-major: element (r, k) at Ld[k * nLoc + r].\n__global__ void kExternal(const double* __restrict__ Ld, int nLoc, int rStart,\n                          const double* __restrict__ piv, int ldp, int j0, int w,\n                          double* __restrict__ accE) {\n    const int r = rStart + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int c = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (r >= nLoc || c >= w) return;\n    const double* pc = piv + static_cast<size_t>(c) * ldp;\n    double s = 0.0;\n    for (int k = 0; k < j0; ++k) s += Ld[static_cast<size_t>(k) * nLoc + r] * pc[k];\n    accE[static_cast<size_t>(r) * w + c] = s;\n}\n\n// Finishes the panel columns for local rows r >= rStart (rows below the panel).\n// For each panel column c (in order), the internal sum over panel columns k < c is\n// added to the external partial sum, then L[r][j0+c] = (A - sum) / L[j0+c][j0+c].\n__global__ void kPanelSolve(double* __restrict__ Ld, int nLoc, int rStart, int j0, int w,\n                            const double* __restrict__ accE,\n                            const double* __restrict__ Lp,\n                            const double* __restrict__ Ldiag) {\n    const int r = rStart + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (r >= nLoc) return;\n    for (int c = 0; c < w; ++c) {\n        double sum = accE[static_cast<size_t>(r) * w + c];\n        for (int k = 0; k < c; ++k) {\n            sum += Ld[static_cast<size_t>(j0 + k) * nLoc + r] * Lp[c * w + k];\n        }\n        double& dst = Ld[static_cast<size_t>(j0 + c) * nLoc + r];\n        dst = (dst - sum) / Ldiag[c];\n    }\n}\n\n// Writes the factored panel block (lower triangle incl. diagonal) into the rows\n// owned by this rank. Grid: w blocks (panel rows), w threads (panel columns).\n__global__ void kWritePanelBlock(double* __restrict__ Ld, int nLoc, int j0, int w,\n                                 int rank, int size, const double* __restrict__ Lp) {\n    const int cp = blockIdx.x;  // panel row\n    const int c = threadIdx.x;  // panel column\n    if (cp >= w || c > cp) return;\n    const int j = j0 + cp;\n    if (j % size != rank) return;\n    const int lr = (j - rank) / size;\n    Ld[static_cast<size_t>(j0 + c) * nLoc + lr] = Lp[cp * w + c];\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Host-side helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Factors the w x w panel diagonal block on the host. Executed identically on all\n// ranks (inputs are replicated), so every rank reaches the same decision.\n//   piv:    replicated pivot data, row-major with leading dimension ldp; the\n//           panel block of original A is at piv[r * ldp + j0 + c].\n//   accD:   external partial sums for the panel block (lower triangle).\n// Outputs: Lp (w x w row-major, lower triangle, diagonal holds Ldiag) and Ldiag.\nbool factorPanel(const double* piv, size_t ldp, size_t j0, size_t w, const double* accD,\n                 double* Lp, double* Ldiag, int rank) {\n    std::fill(Lp, Lp + w * w, 0.0);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < w; ++c) {\n        for (size_t r = c; r < w; ++r) {\n            double sum = accD[r * w + c];\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < c; ++k) sum += Lp[r * w + k] * Lp[c * w + k];\n            if (r == c) {\n                const double val = piv[c * ldp + j0 + c] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    if (rank == 0) {\n                        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\",\n                               j0 + c);\n                    }\n                    return false;\n                }\n                Ldiag[c] = sqrt(val);\n                Lp[c * w + c] = Ldiag[c];\n            } else {\n                Lp[r * w + c] = (piv[r * ldp + j0 + c] - sum) / Ldiag[c];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Device and host scratch buffers reused across panels.\nstruct Workspace {\n    double* dPiv = nullptr;\n    double* dAccD = nullptr;\n    double* dAccE = nullptr;\n    double* dLp = nullptr;\n    double* dLdiag = nullptr;\n    double* hPiv = nullptr;\n    double* hAccD = nullptr;\n    double* hLp = nullptr;\n    double* hLdiag = nullptr;\n\n    Workspace(size_t n, size_t nLoc) {\n        const size_t w = std::min(kPanel, std::max<size_t>(n, 1));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dPiv, sizeof(double) * w * std::max<size_t>(n, 1)));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dAccD, sizeof(double) * w * w));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dAccE, sizeof(double) * std::max<size_t>(nLoc * w, 1)));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dLp, sizeof(double) * w * w));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dLdiag, sizeof(double) * w));\n        hPiv = new double[w * std::max<size_t>(n, 1)];\n        hAccD = new double[w * w];\n        hLp = new double[w * w];\n        hLdiag = new double[w];\n    }\n\n    ~Workspace() {\n        cudaFree(dPiv);\n        cudaFree(dAccD);\n        cudaFree(dAccE);\n        cudaFree(dLp);\n        cudaFree(dLdiag);\n        delete[] hPiv;\n        delete[] hAccD;\n        delete[] hLp;\n        delete[] hLdiag;\n    }\n\n    Workspace(const Workspace&) = delete;\n    Workspace& operator=(const Workspace&) = delete;\n};\n\n// Distributed in-place Cholesky of the column-major device matrix dL.\n// dL holds this rank's rows: element (local row r, column k) at dL[k * nLoc + r].\n// Returns false if the matrix is not positive definite (same result on all ranks).\nbool choleskyDecomposition(double* dL, size_t n, int rank, int size, size_t nLoc,\n                           Workspace& ws) {\n    const int nl = static_cast<int>(nLoc);\n    const int ni = static_cast<int>(n);\n    const size_t dataDouble = sizeof(double);\n\n    for (int j0 = 0; j0 < ni; j0 += static_cast<int>(kPanel)) {\n        const int j1 = std::min(ni, j0 + static_cast<int>(kPanel));\n        const int w = j1 - j0;\n        const int ldp = j0 + w;  // row stride of the pivot buffer\n\n        // 1. Owners of panel rows export their factored prefix (columns < j0) and\n        //    their original panel block (columns j0..j1-1). Other entries stay zero.\n        std::memset(ws.hPiv, 0, dataDouble * static_cast<size_t>(w) * ldp);\n        for (int c = 0; c < w; ++c) {\n            const int j = j0 + c;\n            if (j % size != rank) continue;\n            const size_t lr = static_cast<size_t>(j - rank) / size;\n            double* dst = ws.hPiv + static_cast<size_t>(c) * ldp;\n            if (j0 > 0) {\n                CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy2D(dst, dataDouble, dL + lr, nLoc * dataDouble, dataDouble,\n                                        static_cast<size_t>(j0), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n            }\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy2D(dst + j0, dataDouble, dL + static_cast<size_t>(j0) * nLoc + lr,\n                                    nLoc * dataDouble, dataDouble, static_cast<size_t>(w),\n                                    cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n\n        // 2. Replicate the pivot panel on all ranks (exactly one owner per row,\n        //    so the sum reproduces the owner's values).\n        MPI_Allreduce(MPI_IN_PLACE, ws.hPiv, w * ldp, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_SUM, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(ws.dPiv, ws.hPiv, dataDouble * w * ldp, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n        // 3. External partial sums of the panel diagonal block, then factor it on host.\n        {\n            dim3 block(16, 16);\n            dim3 grid((w + 15) / 16, (w + 15) / 16);\n            kPivotDiag<<<grid, block>>>(ws.dPiv, ldp, j0, w, ws.dAccD);\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(ws.hAccD, ws.dAccD, dataDouble * w * w, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        if (!factorPanel(ws.hPiv, static_cast<size_t>(ldp), static_cast<size_t>(j0),\n                         static_cast<size_t>(w), ws.hAccD, ws.hLp, ws.hLdiag, rank)) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(ws.dLp, ws.hLp, dataDouble * w * w, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(ws.dLdiag, ws.hLdiag, dataDouble * w, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n        // 4. Rows below the panel (global index >= j1), owned locally.\n        const int rStart = (j1 > rank) ? (j1 - rank + size - 1) / size : 0;\n        if (rStart < nl) {\n            const int rows = nl - rStart;\n            dim3 block(32, 8);\n            dim3 grid((rows + 31) / 32, (w + 7) / 8);\n            kExternal<<<grid, block>>>(dL, nl, rStart, ws.dPiv, ldp, j0, w, ws.dAccE);\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n\n            kPanelSolve<<<(rows + 127) / 128, 128>>>(dL, nl, rStart, j0, w, ws.dAccE, ws.dLp,\n                                                     ws.dLdiag);\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n\n        // 5. Panel rows owned locally: write the factored panel block.\n        kWritePanelBlock<<<w, w>>>(dL, nl, j0, w, rank, size, ws.dLp);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate this rank's rows of A = B * B^T + n * I, where B is pseudo-random.\n// B is generated identically on every rank (same sequence as the sequential code).\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& Arow, size_t n, int rank, int size,\n                                    size_t nLoc) {\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute local rows of A = B * B^T (row-major local storage)\n    Arow.assign(nLoc * n, 0.0);\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic)\n    for (long long rr = 0; rr < static_cast<long long>(nLoc); ++rr) {\n        const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rr);\n        const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank) + r * static_cast<size_t>(size);\n        const double* bi = &B[i * n];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double* bj = &B[j * n];\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += bi[k] * bj[k];\n            }\n            Arow[r * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n        // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n        Arow[r * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\n// Distributed validation: reconstruct L * L^T for local rows and compare with A.\n// Row blocks of L circulate around a ring so each rank sees every block of L once.\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& Lrow, const std::vector<double>& Aorig,\n                      size_t n, int rank, int size, size_t nLoc) {\n    const size_t maxLoc = localRowCount(n, 0, size);\n    std::vector<double> cur(maxLoc * n, 0.0);\n    std::vector<double> nxt(maxLoc * n, 0.0);\n    std::copy(Lrow.begin(), Lrow.end(), cur.begin());\n\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    for (int step = 0; step < size; ++step) {\n        const int owner = (rank - step + size) % size;\n        const size_t cnt = localRowCount(n, owner, size);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic) reduction(max : maxError) reduction(max : relError)\n        for (long long rr = 0; rr < static_cast<long long>(nLoc); ++rr) {\n            const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rr);\n            const double* li = &Lrow[r * n];\n            for (size_t s = 0; s < cnt; ++s) {\n                const size_t j = static_cast<size_t>(owner) + s * static_cast<size_t>(size);\n                const double* lj = &cur[s * n];\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) sum += li[k] * lj[k];\n                const double orig = Aorig[r * n + j];\n                const double error = fabs(sum - orig);\n                maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n                const double rel = error / (fabs(orig) + 1e-10);\n                relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (size > 1 && step + 1 < size) {\n            const int src = (rank - step - 1 + size) % size;\n            const size_t nextCnt = localRowCount(n, src, size);\n            MPI_Sendrecv(cur.data(), static_cast<int>(cnt * n), MPI_DOUBLE, (rank + 1) % size, 0,\n                         nxt.data(), static_cast<int>(nextCnt * n), MPI_DOUBLE,\n                         (rank - 1 + size) % size, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);\n            std::swap(cur, nxt);\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Allreduce(MPI_IN_PLACE, &maxError, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    MPI_Allreduce(MPI_IN_PLACE, &relError, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n        printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    }\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        if (rank == 0) printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    (void)nLoc;\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv, int rank, int size) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Bind each rank to a GPU (ranks on the same node are numbered locally)\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        if (rank == 0) fprintf(stderr, \"Error: no CUDA devices available\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaSetDevice(localRank % deviceCount));\n\n    // Divide hardware threads among the ranks sharing this node\n    omp_set_num_threads(std::max(1, omp_get_num_procs() / localSize));\n\n    const size_t nLoc = localRowCount(n, rank, size);\n\n    // Generate local rows (row-major)\n    if (rank == 0) printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    std::vector<double> Arow;\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(Arow, n, rank, size, nLoc);\n\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = Arow;  // Save original local rows for validation\n    }\n\n    // Upload to device in column-major layout: element (r, k) at k * nLoc + r\n    double* dL = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dL, sizeof(double) * std::max<size_t>(nLoc * n, 1)));\n    {\n        std::vector<double> Acm(nLoc * n);\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (long long kk = 0; kk < static_cast<long long>(n); ++kk) {\n            const size_t k = static_cast<size_t>(kk);\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < nLoc; ++r) Acm[k * nLoc + r] = Arow[r * n + k];\n        }\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dL, Acm.data(), sizeof(double) * nLoc * n, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n    std::vector<double>().swap(Arow);\n\n    Workspace ws(n, nLoc);\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    if (rank == 0) printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    const bool success = choleskyDecomposition(dL, n, rank, size, nLoc, ws);\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        if (rank == 0) printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        cudaFree(dL);\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n        double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n        double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Copy factor back to host and build row-major local rows with zero upper part\n    std::vector<double> Lrow(nLoc * n);\n    {\n        std::vector<double> Lcm(nLoc * n);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(Lcm.data(), dL, sizeof(double) * nLoc * n, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (long long rr = 0; rr < static_cast<long long>(nLoc); ++rr) {\n            const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rr);\n            const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(rank) + r * static_cast<size_t>(size);\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                Lrow[r * n + k] = (k <= i) ? Lcm[k * nLoc + r] : 0.0;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    cudaFree(dL);\n\n    // Gather full L on rank 0 for external-validation output\n    if (printResults) {\n        const size_t total = n * n;\n        std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n        for (int q = 0; q < size; ++q) {\n            counts[q] = static_cast<int>(localRowCount(n, q, size) * n);\n            displs[q] = (q == 0) ? 0 : displs[q - 1] + counts[q - 1];\n        }\n        std::vector<double> gathered(rank == 0 ? total : 0);\n        MPI_Gatherv(Lrow.data(), static_cast<int>(nLoc * n), MPI_DOUBLE, gathered.data(),\n                    counts.data(), displs.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            std::vector<double> L(total);\n            for (int q = 0; q < size; ++q) {\n                const size_t cnt = localRowCount(n, q, size);\n                for (size_t s = 0; s < cnt; ++s) {\n                    const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(q) + s * static_cast<size_t>(size);\n                    std::copy_n(gathered.begin() + displs[q] + s * n, n, L.begin() + i * n);\n                }\n            }\n            print_results(L, \"CholeskyL\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        if (rank == 0) printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(Lrow, A_orig, n, rank, size, nLoc);\n\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            if (valid) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            }\n        }\n        return valid ? 0 : 1;\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int ret = runBenchmark(argc, argv, rank, size);\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return ret;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793006051906,"end":1793006051999}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1777caf130016HvFNKlojOaaAx","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","messageID":"msg_1777ca114001AVYK4hCUTfmslc"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793006689402,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_17786bd0e001Q6NLID7VAHr19J","messageID":"msg_17786b0ed001a6jStNLNYE1j0b","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"At n=2048, the speedup is dramatic: 2152 ms down to 234 ms with np=1, a 9x gain. But np=2 hits 150 ms while np=4 actually slows to 202 ms, which is odd — I'm wondering if that's from allreduce sync overhead across the 4 GPUs or some host-side factor specific to that rank count, since the OpenMP thread split (64 per rank) shouldn't matter here. I want to figure out what's actually bottlenecking this case.\n\nEach panel involves blocking device transfers, an allreduce, and compute kernels. Doing a rough FLOP count, the ideal runtime should be around 10 ms, but we're seeing 234 ms — roughly 25x slower than ideal, suggesting a memory-bound or latency-bound kernel rather than compute-bound. My suspicion is that kPanelSolve is the culprit: with only 2048 threads active across 82 SMs, and a dependent accumulation chain forcing serialized global memory loads, the kernel is likely latency-bound rather than throughput-bound. I should profile this with nsys or ncu to confirm where the time is actually going.\n\nChecking kExternal's thread count confirms it's fine (131k threads, well-parallelized), so the fix needs to focus on kPanelSolve — trying to reduce per-thread global memory latency by caching row values in registers or shared memory instead of repeated global loads, while being careful about register pressure and handling the variable panel width at the last iteration.\n\nRather than overengineering this, I think the practical move is to profile first — check if nsys or ncu is available to actually measure where time is going before optimizing further.\n\n","time":{"start":1793006681358,"end":1793006689356},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I'm thinking through ways to restructure kPanelSolve for better per-thread work distribution.\n\nThat math only gets to 16ms total, far short of the observed 234ms, so the bottleneck must be elsewhere. I'm now suspecting the cudaMemcpy2D calls for transferring owned rows — with tiny 8-byte widths and strided sources, these likely decompose into thousands of individual small DMA transfers per panel, which could easily dominate the runtime instead of the compute itself.\n\nThe clean fix is to pack data on the device first using a kernel that writes the pivot rows into a contiguous staging buffer, then do a single D2H transfer of the whole block instead of many strided memcpy2D calls. Rows owned by other\n// ranks are written as zero, so an element-wise sum across ranks replicates them.\n// Grid: (ceil(ldp / blockDim.x), w).\n__global__ void kPackPanel(const double* __restrict__ Ld, int nLoc, int j0, int w, int ldp,\n                           int rank, int size, double* __restrict__ stage) {\n    const int k = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int c = blockIdx.y;\n    if (k >= ldp || c >= w) return;\n    const int j = j0 + c;\n    double v = 0.0;\n    if (j % size == rank) {\n        const int lr = (j - rank) / size;\n        v = Ld[static_cast<size_t>(k) * nLoc + lr];\n    }\n    stage[static_cast<size_t>(c) * ldp + k] = v;\n}\n\n// Finishes the panel columns for local rows r >= rStart (rows below the panel)."},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp\n@@ -84,8 +84,26 @@\n     for (int k = 0; k < j0; ++k) s += Ld[static_cast<size_t>(k) * nLoc + r] * pc[k];\n     accE[static_cast<size_t>(r) * w + c] = s;\n }\n \n+// Packs the panel rows owned by this rank into a row-major staging buffer\n+// stage[c * ldp + k] = A/L[j0 + c][k] for k < ldp (ldp = j1). {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008091017,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_1779c240f0015myf9T43jhzeGB","messageID":"msg_1779c1c30001mF1BWQg7f4yQoA","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"Looking at the timing breakdown, kGenerate's 255ms isn't critical since it's untimed, kExternal at 40ms is solid, and kPivotDiag's 18ms could be improved by addressing the uncoalesced global memory reads in the w² threads, though it's a minor 5% contributor. The decomposition totals roughly 75ms plus host overhead, which roughly matches the 107ms measured earlier.\n\nChecking where the rest of the time goes: likely host syncs and allreduce per panel across 64 panels with D2H/H2D transfers, which seems reasonable. Working through kExternal's FMA count, I estimate it's doing roughly n³/6 FMAs in 40ms, which translates to about 0.57 TFLOPS — remarkably close to the 3090's FP64 peak of ~0.556 TFLOPS (since FP64 runs at 1/64 of the 35.6 TFLOPS FP32 rate). That means kExternal is essentially compute-bound at hardware peak already, which is a great sign since the total algorithm flops are fixed at n³/3.\n\nNow I want to look at multi-GPU scaling behavior — earlier np=2 gave 29ms vs np=1's 26ms, so I'm setting up a background script to measure n=4096 across 1, 2, 3, and 4 ranks with 3 repetitions each, keeping in mind mpirun's default process binding might affect things.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008083983,"end":1793008090953},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008226202,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_1779e097a001XtA3oa6w1JuV9L","messageID":"msg_1779e00ee001vb4dqllTtORf2P","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm puzzling over why scaling is so poor—np=2 shows no speedup over np=1 at 4096, and np=3 is even worse. I suspect the per-panel fixed overhead from allreduce latency and D2H/H2D sync costs is dominating, since np=1 avoids the MPI allreduce entirely while np=2/3 pay that cost across all 64 panels.\n\nThe real culprit is data volume: the replicated pivot panel moves roughly 67 MB of doubles through allreduce per rank, which over shared-memory transports could easily cost 50-130 ms given typical intra-node bandwidth, dwarfing the much cheaper D2H/H2D transfers. A better approach would only communicate the panel rows actually owned by distinct ranks rather than replicating the full prefix.\n\nInstead of allreduce, I should use allgatherv so each rank contributes just its owned rows (determined by the cyclic distribution over the panel's column range), cutting redundant computation and reducing passes compared to the reduce-scatter-plus-allgather pattern allreduce performs internally.\n\nI pack owned rows into a compact staging buffer on the host, allgatherv them, then unpack by computing each row's owner and offset to restore the correct row ordering — a cheap host-side copy. I briefly consider whether CUDA-aware MPI could skip the host round trip, but I'm unsure it's supported here, so I'll avoid relying on it and keep the pipeline as D2H pack, allgatherv, H2D, then kernels.\n\nLooking at timing, the np=2 case still costs roughly 20-30ms in communication even as GPU work drops by half, and np=3 at 278ms suggests the allreduce's sum algorithm scales poorly across ranks — replacing it with allgatherv should help more than per-row broadcasts, which would be too latency-heavy. I also consider overlapping communication with the next panel's pivot packing but set that aside as too complex for now.\n\nFor implementation, I'm defining row ownership as j%size, computing per-rank row counts, and designing a pack kernel that writes each owned row into its compacted slot position.\n\nDefining the unpack and transfer logic...\n\nSince the recv order groups by rank, I'm fine keeping the host-side unpack. Now I'm working out the owned row count formula per rank, computing c0 as a modular offset from the rank relative to j0, and double-checking that derivation.\n\nFor edge cases, I need Allgatherv to handle ranks with zero owned rows correctly (zero counts, skipped pack/D2H, and valid buffer pointers even when size is zero). I'm also verifying the local row index computation—making sure j, derived from j0+c, stays consistent with rank modulo size without going negative.\n\nNow I'm writing a kernel to pack owned panel columns, then plan the host-side unpacking logic that reconstructs the full panel from each rank's received segment using per-rank offsets and strides, followed by copying the assembled panel back to the device for the subsequent kernels that expect the layout column-major by ldp.\n\nFor workspace, I need to allocate separate send and receive buffers sized for the panel (since Allgatherv requires distinct in/out arrays), sized conservatively at width times ldp, then proceed with the implementation.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008208250,"end":1793008226138},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793008226203,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_1779e4f5d001HHTkO46wRYTDMc","messageID":"msg_1779e00ee001vb4dqllTtORf2P","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"text","text":"Scaling is poor. Two GPUs barely beat one at n=4096, and three are much slower. The cause is the per-panel `MPI_Allreduce`. It sums zero-filled buffers across all ranks, which costs about twice the necessary traffic plus host reduction work, and that is paid on every panel.\n\nEach panel row has exactly one owner, so an `MPI_Allgatherv` of each rank's owned rows is the right collective. Each rank then sends only its own rows, and the receive volume is the minimum the algorithm needs. I'll pack the owned rows compactly on the device, gather them, and unpack on the host.","time":{"start":1793008226141,"end":1793008226155}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008564163,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177a35c760014fgG6pw0SK2Bfi","messageID":"msg_177a3538f0010h72z4R7kRKaOD","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"Scaling still isn't improving at n=4096 despite np=3/4 gains—np=2 matches np=1, and np=4 only reaches 162-185. I suspect the bottleneck is latency from per-panel synchronization: each panel requires a pack kernel, synchronous device-to-host transfer, an allgatherv where ranks stall waiting on each other due to workload imbalance, then host-to-device transfer, diagonal pivoting, another D2H, host-side factorization, and more transfers before the external kernel runs.\n\nWith 64 panels, even small per-panel costs add up fast. Quantifying this: np=1 takes 96-104ms total with kernels around 75ms, leaving ~20ms sync overhead. But np=4 shows kernel work dropping to ~19ms while total time balloons to 160ms, implying ~140ms of communication/latency overhead across 64 panels—roughly 2.2ms per panel, which seems excessive. I'm wondering if this points to a slow MPI_Allgatherv implementation, host factorization stalls, or memcpy synchronization issues, though with one process per GPU that shouldn't be the culprit. I'm also considering whether CPU binding or OpenMP thread contention could be adding overhead, though OpenMP isn't actually used in this decomposition path.\n\nI should profile np=4 with nsys to get a real breakdown—tracing CUDA, OS runtime, and MPI events to isolate where the time is going, particularly looking at MPI_Allgatherv durations and cudaMemcpy wait times via the stats summaries.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008557175,"end":1793008564116},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008634631,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177a43034001SKwXzV4sZxZUgZ","messageID":"msg_177a4274a001s2lAO49vOJWTua","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"The raw allgatherv of 512KB/rank is clocking around 1ms for np=4, which seems to be the floor for this MPI library's transport, but our per-call average is running higher at 1.6ms once panel waits are included — so communication is clearly the bottleneck for np≥3. I'm thinking through ways to cut this down, starting with reducing how much pivot panel data each rank actually needs replicated for its local GEMM work.\n\nFor n=4096, each rank ends up receiving roughly 67MB total across the factorization given the n²/2 scaling, which at ~0.5GB/s translates to about 130ms — that's inherent to the row-cyclic layout with replicated pivots. I'm weighing whether a 2D block-cyclic distribution could help instead, splitting both rows and columns across a p×q rank grid so each rank only needs a fraction of the pivot data and partial GEMM sums get reduced across just the q ranks in its row — though I need to be careful that the summation order over k stays consistent to preserve bitwise reproducibility.\n\nReducing over k-partitions would break strict ordering, giving only tolerance-level equality rather than bitwise identical results — this is a real tradeoff since floating-point reassociation is technically valid under \"equivalent semantics\" but I'd prefer to preserve bitwise equality if possible. So I'm now looking at overlapping communication instead: pipelining the pivot exchange with computation so panel p+1's required pivot rows can start updating while panel p is still finishing its work, accumulating contributions in ascending k order across panels to keep the result deterministic.\n\nRealizing I could maintain a full n×n accumulator per process, folding in each panel's contribution as it's computed — this makes the ascending-order accumulation automatic, but doubles memory since it's the same size as L itself. The upside is that communication per panel then shrinks to just the small w×w block of newly computed pivot values, since everything before that panel is already folded into the accumulator and doesn't need to be re-sent.\n\nThe flop count per panel stays the same as before—a GEMM of the accumulator against future columns—so the total still hits n³/3, and the accumulation order is preserved since each acc entry sums k in ascending order across panels. What the panel factor actually needs is just the local diagonal block, the accumulated external contributions for that block, and the original panel data from its owner—nothing beyond that, since all earlier k-contributions are already folded into the accumulator.\n\nBut here's the real problem: updating the accumulator for all future columns requires L-values from every future row, not merely the next panel's pivot rows. That means the entire panel column of width w must be broadcast to all ranks, which brings the communication volume straight back up to n² total—exactly the kind of all-to-all replication a 1D row-distributed layout seems to force, since each rank ultimately needs every row of L to finish its local updates.\n\nActually that n² total volume per rank is just inherent to 1D distribution; a 2D block-cyclic layout like ScaLAPACK would instead bring it down to O(n²/√P), since each rank only needs the prefix of the rows and columns it owns rather than the full matrix—so I should weigh accepting the 1D cost versus moving to a 2D distribution that preserves the same per-element computation order.\n\nFor modest P the 2D gain is weak (P=4 gives no improvement at all, since each rank still needs n²/2), only becoming meaningful at larger P like 16 where volume halves. Given the added complexity for a win only at scale, it doesn't seem worth it, so I'm accepting the n²/2 doubling as inherent and instead checking whether the measured timings match—back-of-envelope bandwidth estimates suggest the actual Allgatherv overhead is roughly 3x what raw bandwidth predicts, meaning most of the gap is synchronization skew across the pipeline (pack, D2H, allgather, H2D, diagonal factor) rather than pure data volume. I'm now considering whether using larger panel widths could reduce the number of syncs without changing total volume, trading per-panel latency overhead for slightly less parallelism per step.\n\nTesting panel widths of 128 and 256 should be a trivial constant change since the kernels and workspace already support arbitrary widths up to 1024, and the host-side factorization cost stays negligible at these sizes. I also consider whether non-blocking MPI overlap could hide communication behind GPU compute, but tracing the dependency chain shows the next panel's pack depends on only-partially-overlapping work from the current panel, making true overlap complex enough to set aside for now. Pinned memory might help marginally, so the plan is to just try the panel-width change first and remeasure, while confirming that row distribution across ranks stays balanced.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008611380,"end":1793008634524},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008754962,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177a61e72001cCOunuoKzhrbKS","messageID":"msg_177a616b8001GhUGqIOHeXBbe5","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"The timing gain isn't huge, and results are noisy—141 vs 96 for the same binary earlier. I suspect communication and synchronization dominate the critical path per panel for np=4: packing and D2H sync, the allgatherv call taking over a millisecond, H2D transfer, pivot diagonal with another sync, the host-side factorization, then H2D for Lp and Ldiag before the final exchange step.\n\nAt np=4 each GPU handles roughly a quarter of the work, about 20ms of kernel time total, but the overall run is ~150ms, meaning ~130ms is comm/sync overhead—around 2ms per panel across 64 panels. Since the raw allgatherv is only ~1ms, the remaining ~1ms per panel comes from syncs, rank skew, and host overhead like the unpack memcpy (roughly 2MB per panel, ~0.3ms) plus the H2D transfer. I'm considering a software pipelining approach: overlapping the comm for panel p+1 with the GPU work for panel p, since the pivot rows needed for the next panel's allgather are already computed by the owners during the current panel's solve step—so there's a real dependency chain to work through here.\n\nOne idea is to split the kernel work using two streams: a small kernel first computes just the rows needed for the next panel's pack/download (critical path), while the bulk of the remaining rows run asynchronously in a second stream. This could hide most of the GPU time behind communication, though it gets a bit involved since the owner-local row indices for the next panel are scattered in a cyclic pattern, requiring care to identify the right contiguous ranges per rank.\n\nI'm working through the dependency ordering per panel: wait for the bulk stream from the previous panel to finish (since all rows need updating before pivoting), do the pivot exchange, factor on host, send the factored panel back to device, then launch the next round of row updates — alternating between the critical-path stream and the bulk stream to keep overlap working correctly.\n\nI also need to watch for a subtle hazard: the staging buffer used to pack the panel for broadcast is the same one consumed by the external-update kernel reading pivot data, so writing new pack data for the next panel could race with the current panel's kernel still reading it — I need to make sure that's properly sequenced rather than just relying on stream order.\n\nWith this pipeline the critical path per panel shrinks to the small kernels plus D2H, allgather, H2D, and the diagonal/host factorization step, while the bulk compute overlaps the communication. Given roughly 0.3ms of bulk compute versus ~1ms of comm per panel at four ranks, this is still comm-bound but should yield maybe a 30-40% improvement overall, so I'm now questioning whether the bottleneck is really the MPI transport choice (vader vs tcp) given it's running on a single node.\n\nI'm weighing whether this pipelining effort is worthwhile given the current scaling numbers look weak — at n=4096 four GPUs barely beats one, and at n=8192 times go from 524ms (np=1) to 400ms (np=2) with unclear np=3/4 results I need to check in the log. Estimating communication volume at n=8192 (~268MB per rank at 1.5GB/s ≈ 180ms) against expected GPU compute of ~125ms at np=4 suggests a predicted total near 300ms, which I want to verify against the actual measured log output. This points to the comm volume being an inherent limitation of the 1D decomposition — a 2D approach wouldn't help much at small P — so I'm now considering whether the pivot panel broadcast could be restructured to reduce the total P × n²/2 data movement from the allgather.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008737906,"end":1793008754906},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793008818477,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177a73548001jDlFDlSKx7eDQ3","messageID":"msg_177a72b2000127I5AMI4o4Pgm3","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"The scaling looks poor—at n=8192 with 4 processes it's roughly the same time as a single GPU, so communication overhead must be dominating. I'm estimating the data volume: each rank handles around 200 MB of doubles, which at typical interconnect speeds would add on the order of 135 ms just for transfer, plus additional host-to-device and device-to-host copy overhead.\n\nThe full pivot panel transfer is around 268 MB per rank over PCIe, adding roughly 27-50 ms more for copies and unpacking, bringing the comm-related total to around 250 ms, plus ~130 ms compute per rank, landing near the observed 460 ms. So the real bottleneck is the replication volume and the host-device copy overhead. To fix this I'm considering whether the MPI build is actually CUDA-aware (checking ompi_info for CUDA support), which would let Allgatherv operate directly on device buffers and eliminate the extra host staging copies.\n\nI'm also thinking about avoiding the host unpack entirely by passing a row-offset array into the kernels so they can index directly into the gathered buffer without rearranging it on the host first — this removes the ~50ms memcpy but still needs the H2D transfer. Beyond that, pipelining to overlap communication with GPU compute seems necessary, since fundamentally this 1D distribution is communication-heavy with a poor flop-to-byte ratio.\n\nWorking through the numbers, comm and compute costs per panel come out comparable (~1.3ms vs ~2ms), so full overlap could roughly double throughput. Given the effort tradeoff, I think it's worth checking for CUDA-aware MPI support to eliminate extra PCIe copies, while treating full pipelining as a nice-to-have that I may just document rather than implement.\n\n","time":{"start":1793008809288,"end":1793008818435},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Staging through host memory is likely a large share of the cost. I'll check whether this Open MPI build is CUDA-aware, which would let MPI read and write device buffers directly.","time":{"start":1793008818438,"end":1793008818448}}}

For pinned staging, I'll switch hSend/hRecv allocation to cudaMallocHost and make sure to free them with cudaFreeHost.\n\nNow I'm reworking the kernels to index rows through a new rowOff array instead of multiplying by ldp directly — kPivotDiag and kExternal both need a rowOff pointer parameter added, with a corresponding device buffer dRowOff (plus host-side hRowOff) added to the workspace and refreshed via a host-to-device copy each panel. I need to double check the displs/counts math lines up with this compact layout, and that kWritePanelBlock, kPanelSolve, and kPivotDiag's accD indexing stay unchanged since those aren't affected by the row-addressing change.\n\nI'm also switching hSend/hRecv to pinned memory via cudaMallocHost (sized to the max panel elements), using cudaFreeHost to release them, so the H2D copy of the allgathered buffer into dPiv is faster. {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793009338748,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177af49760018epdN0K6wonMBR","messageID":"msg_177af3f55001OceQiThqP8vj3x","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793009361144,"sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","part":{"id":"prt_177af4979001GEItbX5C1nr7x4","messageID":"msg_177af3f55001OceQiThqP8vj3x","sessionID":"ses_e888819b9ffecY0D9ip9GLYX52","type":"reasoning","text":"Looking at the allgatherv timings, 192 calls average 1.36 ms but the max spikes to 8.7 ms, pointing to real skew between ranks rather than uniform cost — some ranks are finishing their GPU work later, probably because the per-panel workload isn't actually balanced evenly across ranks.\n\nThe deeper problem is that GPU compute and host communication are fully serialized per panel: each rank does its kernel work, then packs and does a D2H copy that blocks until the GPU queue drains, then waits for allgatherv — so there's zero overlap between bulk compute and communication. With np=3, rough math (31ms bulk + 87ms comm ≈ 118ms) doesn't even match the measured 155ms, so overlap via pipelining next-panel rows could roughly recover 1.5-2x, but it's a meaningful engineering lift for a moderate payoff.\n\nGiven the effort already spent, I'm weighing a simpler compromise: split kernel work within each panel across two streams, computing rows needed by the next panel first (so packing/H2D can start sooner) while the remaining rows continue on a second stream — but this introduces subtle synchronization dependencies between streams that need careful ordering to avoid races on shared pivot data.\n\nI'm realizing I need double buffering for the pivot data, L-panel/diagonal buffers, and the write-block kernel outputs, since both streams can be working on different panels' data simultaneously and would otherwise overwrite each other. I'm also tracing through the cross-stream ordering carefully to confirm that each panel's kernels correctly wait on the prior panel's writes to the same rows and columns before reading them.\n\nOverall this change is maybe 60 lines, moderate risk, with existing bitwise tests for verification — but the expected gain is limited: hiding the ~30ms bulk GPU time only helps when comm (~87ms) dominates, capping the improvement around 25-30%, not transformative. I'm now looking at whether the real bottleneck is actually the allgather communication itself — the per-panel allgather averages 1.36ms but has a minimum of 0.11ms, suggesting load skew between ranks is causing ranks to wait on each other even though their GPU work looks similar.\n\nGiven the time I have, I'll stop trying to further optimize the multi-GPU pipeline and be honest in the summary: single-GPU scales near-linearly, but multi-GPU gains are limited on this node because each panel does an MPI allgather of O(n²) total data through host memory (not CUDA-aware), with synchronous per-panel stages — I'll flag this clearly as a scalability bottleneck.
